title: Migration
summary: Engage, PureConnect, and Cisco UCCE move by rebuilding Architect flows and queues. This is a learning bridge, not a converter.

lessons.title: Nothing imports your old routing by magic
lessons.summary: You rebuild flows, queues, and trunks. You do not flip a converter this lab has not found.
paras: Genesys Engage routing strategies and PureConnect handlers do not become Architect flows because a project plan says “migrate”. This lab has not found a documented one-click import. The work is to redraw the caller journey in Architect, recreate queues, and point numbers at the new routes. The migration studio in this lab is a table of those mappings, not a tool that edits either platform.

Cisco UCCE, UCCX, and a CUCM or Webex Calling trunk are a different vendor. The bridge lessons cite Cisco’s product pages for what you are leaving and Genesys articles for what you are building. They are not a statement that the platforms are equivalent.
lessons.uncertainty: Lifecycle dates for Engage and PureConnect must be confirmed on Genesys notices. This lesson does not set one.

lessons.title: Engage and PureConnect become flows and queues
lessons.summary: Strategies, IRDs, and handlers are read as behavior, then redrawn.
paras: Treat a Genesys Engage routing strategy or IRD as a description of menus, data dips, and targets. Treat PureConnect handlers and queues the same way. The Genesys Cloud objects are Architect flows, including common modules for anything you would otherwise paste twice, and queues with skills and a routing method. Confirm the current PureConnect or Engage lifecycle on a Genesys notice before you put a date in a steering deck. Community dates are not a contract.

Recording policies, WFM, and bots do not come along inside the IVR export. They are separate tracks in this lab because they are separate products. A cutover that only moves prompts has not moved the contact center.

lessons.title: IVR becomes Architect tasks, menus, and audio
lessons.summary: CVP, UCCX prompts, and Engage voice all become the same kind of flow.
paras: Create a flow is the article for the voice tasks you will rebuild: play audio, collect input, decisions, transfers, data actions. Cisco’s UCCX and UCCE pages remain the description of the old script. The mapping is conceptual. A CVP application and a UCCX script both become Architect if the journey is a voice menu. They do not keep their tool names.

In-queue treatment is a separate flow type, and the default in-queue call flow does nothing until you publish it. Migrating “music on hold” is not done when the inbound menu works. Call the queue and sit in it.

lessons.title: UCCE skill groups and precision queues are not Genesys queues
lessons.summary: Membership, skills, and bullseye are three ideas you reassemble.
paras: Cisco’s UCCE pages describe skill groups and precision queues as that product’s targeting. In Genesys Cloud a queue has members, and skills sit on the agents. All-skills matching, best available, and disregard skills are evaluation methods. Bullseye adds up to five rings, a delay from 2 seconds to 72 hours, and removal of up to 50 skills. Preferred agents are a further method. None of these objects is a UCCE skill group.
A precision queue that expands over time is the closest teaching analogy to bullseye. It is an analogy. The limits above are Genesys settings. Quote Cisco’s guide for Cisco’s limits, not these.

lessons.title: UCCX is a smaller center with the same rebuild rule
lessons.summary: Scripts, CSQs, and the Finesse desktop do not move as files.
paras: Cisco’s UCCX series page is the door to that product’s scripts, contact service queues, and agent desktop. In Genesys Cloud the script becomes Architect, the CSQ becomes a queue with members and skills, and the desktop becomes the Genesys workspace or a documented CRM embed such as Salesforce or Zendesk. Finesse gadgets do not install from AppFoundry under a new name unless a listing you open says so.
UCCX customers often have a single site and a CUCM. The trunk lesson is next. Do not start with the trunk. Start with one published flow and one queue, then call it with a test number.

lessons.title: CUCM stays. BYOC is the door, not a replacement cluster.
lessons.summary: A dial plan and a trunk are Genesys number plans and a BYOC trunk. CUCM is still yours.
paras: The migration studio’s CUCM row points at BYOC PBX or BYOC Carrier, and at Dynamic Cloud Voice for new cloud trunks. Genesys does not absorb the CUCM cluster. Extensions, partitions, and calling search spaces stay on the Cisco side until you deliberately move a pattern. Number plans on the Genesys site classify what Genesys sees, up to 200 plans per site, including the emergency classification.

Local route groups and a premises Edge are a different design from a cloud trunk. If phones register to an Edge, use the Edge track. If CUCM sends a SIP trunk to Genesys, use the BYOC track. Do not draw both and configure neither.

lessons.title: Webex is a neighbor, not a page this lab pretends to summarize
lessons.summary: Use Cisco’s product pages. Do not cite a Webex help URL this lab did not confirm.
paras: Webex Contact Center and Webex Calling show up in the same migrations as CUCM. This lab did not confirm a specific Webex help article to deep-link, so it will not invent one. Cisco’s UCCE and UCCX series pages are the Cisco citations already checked. For Webex, say “open the current Cisco or Webex document” and attach it in your own design.

Where Webex Calling is the PBX, the Genesys side is still a BYOC trunk or a premises Edge, plus Architect and queues. The neighbor can change its calling model without Genesys’ articles changing. Re-read both sides in the same week.

lessons.title: Cut over one number, then the queue, then the people
lessons.summary: A weekend big-bang is how untested emergency routes meet a full staff.
paras: Order: a lab number through the new trunk or Edge, the emergency classification tested the way the emergency article allows, one published inbound flow, one published in-queue flow, one queue with real agents On Queue, then a single production number. Fair-use and recording policies should already exist, or you will record nothing and be surprised, or record everything and surprise legal.

Rollback is the old route still in place for every number you have not moved. Do not delete the CUCM pattern or the Engage route as the first step. Write the rollback as a person’s action, with a clock time.
